content:
nina: Heads up - a few users report undici ending up in browser bundles after upgrading the JS SDK. error: 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' in client console.

ben: Typical cause: static imports or referencing Node-only modules from the main entry. We should ensure undici is only dynamically imported at runtime.

kai: Proposed runtime adapter pattern:
```js
export async function getFetch() {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch;
  const { fetch } = await import('undici');
  return fetch;
}
```
This keeps bundlers from pulling undici into browser bundles.

olivia: For CJS consumers show shim: `const { getFetch } = require('./cjs-interop');` where cjs-interop lazily imports the ESM adapter.

nina: Docs should include bundler hints: webpack alias undici->false, Vite: exclude undici from optimizeDeps and mark it external for SSR builds. Also mention Next.js edge functions and Cloudflare Workers have fetch builtin -> do nothing.

ben: TS note: tell users to add "lib":["DOM"] or include a minimal `types/fetch.d.ts` to avoid missing types on server code.

kai: Tests to add: simple Vite build that asserts undici not present in client output, Node 16 runtime test that dynamically imports undici, and a Nextjs edge smoke.

olivia: UX detail: dynamic import adds small cold-start; show `await ensureFetch()` pattern to warm at startup. Also log debug when fallback used.

ci-bot: CI triggered: run/ci/fetch-adapter-checks on branch fetch-adapter-docs (queued).

nina: I'll draft the quickstart page and code samples, will open PR and tag reviewers.
